The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** enabled in your project.  
> * The instance must be launched in a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> * After the instance boots you’ll still need to install the NVIDIA driver (or use the “GPU‑optimized” image that already contains it).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣ Pick a zone that supports GPUs
ZONE="us-central1-b"

# 2️⃣ Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: script to install drivers
```

### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a `startup.sh` file:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install the NVIDIA driver (the latest supported for RTX A6000)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot so the driver loads
reboot
```

Make sure the script is executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), you can POST a JSON payload to the Compute Engine endpoint.

```bash
# Endpoint
URL="https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances"

# JSON body
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# Make the authenticated request (replace YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN)
curl -X POST "$URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Tip**: Use `gcloud auth print-access-token` to obtain a short‑lived token for the curl command.

---

## 3. Verify the instance

Once the instance is running, SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone=$ZONE
```

Inside the VM, confirm the GPU is visible:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Recap

| Step | Command / Action |
|------|------------------|
| 1 | Choose a GPU‑capable zone (`us-central1-b`, etc.) |
| 2 | Run `gcloud compute instances create …` (CLI) **or** POST JSON to the REST endpoint |
| 3 | (Optional) Provide a startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |
| 4 | SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to verify |

That’s all you need to spin up a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS!
